items: CPS 230 took effect on 1 July 2025 (amended version from 1 July 2026) and covers operational risk, business continuity and service providers.
Critical operations need tolerance levels for time, data loss and minimum service, approved by the board.
Notify APRA within 24 hours of a disruption outside tolerance, and within 72 hours of a material operational risk incident.
Material service providers need due diligence, formal agreements, monitoring, an annual register to APRA and fourth-party oversight.
Boards are ultimately responsible; training, testing, audit and reporting give them the evidence they need.

cards.prompt: Which critical operation does your role support, and what would you do in the first hour if it stopped working?

quiz.question: When did APRA's CPS 230 Operational Risk Management first take effect?
options: 1 July 2019
1 January 2024
1 July 2025
31 March 2026
quiz.explanation: CPS 230 took effect on 1 July 2025, replacing the outsourcing and business continuity standards. A version with targeted amendments has applied since 1 July 2026.

quiz.question: Under CPS 230, who must approve the business continuity plan and the tolerance levels for critical operations?
options: APRA
The chief information security officer
The bank's main service provider
The board
quiz.explanation: The board must approve the BCP and tolerance levels, review testing results and oversee the follow-up of findings.

quiz.question: Payments at a bank have been disrupted for longer than the board-approved tolerance. What does CPS 230 require?
options: Notify APRA within 10 business days
Notify APRA as soon as possible and within 24 hours, and report the failure to the board with a remediation plan
Notify APRA only if customers complain
Wait until service is restored, then include the outage in the annual report to APRA and to the board
quiz.explanation: A disruption to a critical operation outside tolerance must be notified within 24 hours. Failures to meet tolerance are also reported to the board with a remediation plan.

quiz.question: A bank's BCP testing program must include which of the following under CPS 230?
options: A full shutdown of all systems every quarter
A test only after an actual disruption
An annual business continuity exercise using severe but plausible scenarios
An exercise designed and run by APRA each year, with the bank observing and recording the results
quiz.explanation: The program must cover all critical operations and include an annual business continuity exercise with severe but plausible scenarios, including provider disruption. APRA may require its own scenario but does not run every exercise.

quiz.question: Which provider must a bank treat as a material service provider under CPS 230, unless it can justify otherwise?
options: A provider of core technology services
The bank's office cleaning contractor
A stationery supplier
A staff canteen operator
quiz.explanation: CPS 230's minimum list for all entities includes risk management, core technology services and internal audit; for a bank it adds credit assessment, funding and liquidity management, and mortgage brokerage.

quiz.question: A bank enters a new agreement with a provider it relies on for a critical operation. When must it notify APRA?
options: Within 24 hours of signing
Only in the annual register
Only if the provider is overseas; domestic providers are reported in the annual register instead
As soon as possible and no later than 20 business days after entering into it
quiz.explanation: CPS 230 requires notice no later than 20 business days after entering into or materially changing such an agreement. Material offshoring needs notice beforehand.

quiz.question: What must a bank do before entering a material offshoring arrangement under CPS 230?
options: Notify APRA before entering into it
Obtain the OAIC's approval
Nothing, if the provider is incorporated in Australia but works offshore
Move all staff offshore with the service
quiz.explanation: APRA must be notified before a material offshoring arrangement. CPS 230 says offshoring includes an Australian-incorporated provider performing the service outside Australia.

quiz.question: A cyber-attack is notified to APRA under CPS 234. It also has a material impact on a critical operation. Must the bank send a separate CPS 230 incident notice?
options: Yes, every incident needs separate CPS 234 and CPS 230 notices, each with its own investigation report attached to it
No, a CPS 234 notice need not be repeated under CPS 230's incident rule, though other CPS 230 duties still apply
No, because CPS 230 does not cover technology risk
Yes, but only after 30 days
quiz.explanation: CPS 230 says an information security incident reported under CPS 234 need not be reported again under its incident notification rule. A tolerance breach and board reporting duties can still apply.

quiz.question: What does CPS 230 require the bank's service provider management policy to address, in addition to direct providers?
options: Risks from fourth parties that material providers rely on for a critical operation
Personal finances of the provider's staff
The provider's marketing strategy and its plans to sell similar services to other banks in Australia
The provider's competitors' pricing
quiz.explanation: The policy must cover entering, monitoring, substituting and exiting material arrangements, managing their risks, and managing risks from fourth parties relied on for critical operations.

quiz.question: After the Medibank incident, what did APRA say it expected regarding accountability?
options: Automatic removal of all directors
No action against individuals, since APRA said accountability sits with the entity and never with its executives
Accountability and consequence management, including executive remuneration impacts where appropriate
Compensation paid by APRA to customers
quiz.explanation: APRA said it expected appropriate accountability and consequence management, including impacts on executive pay where appropriate, plus a review of governance and risk culture.

regulators: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)

references.title: CPS 234 Information Security
references.provision: Board responsibility, roles, capability, policy framework, classification, controls, incident management, testing, internal audit and APRA notification
references.note: Board ultimately responsible; capability and controls commensurate with threats; response plans reviewed and tested annually; APRA told of material incidents within 72 hours and of unremediated material weaknesses within 10 business days.

references.title: CPG 234 Information Security
references.provision: Attachment B (training and awareness); Attachments G and H (testing techniques, board reporting)
references.note: Guidance describing an awareness program for staff, contractors and third parties, tracked and tested on commencement and periodically, covering social engineering and incident reporting.

references.note: Board approves BCP and tolerance levels; APRA told within 72 hours of material operational risk incidents and within 24 hours of a critical operation disrupted outside tolerance; annual BC exercise; material service provider register submitted annually.

bank.question: A regional bank's board delegates all cyber decisions to the CIO and asks for no reporting. Which CPS 234 requirement is the board most clearly failing?
options: Its ultimate responsibility for ensuring security matches the threats and supports sound operation
The duty to notify APRA within 10 business days of every incident, whether material or not, with the board's sign-off
The rule that only directors may approve firewall changes
The duty to classify assets by market value
bank.explanation: CPS 234 makes the board ultimately responsible for information security. Delegating operations is fine; abandoning oversight is not. The other options misstate the standard.

bank.question: A foreign bank operates a branch in Sydney. To which operations do CPS 234's obligations apply?
options: Its worldwide operations, wherever located, because the head office controls the branch
The Australian branch operations of that foreign ADI
None, because foreign banks are exempt
Only systems physically hosted in Australia
bank.explanation: CPS 234 states that its obligations on a foreign ADI apply only in relation to its Australian branch operations.

bank.question: A bank's spreadsheet of branch staff rosters is widely shared and rarely needed in a hurry. How is it most likely classified under CPS 234?
options: High criticality, because all data is critical
Outside CPS 234, because it is a spreadsheet
Low sensitivity and low criticality, so lighter controls are commensurate
High sensitivity, because any file that contains staff names must be protected at the highest level
bank.explanation: Classification reflects the impact of losing availability (criticality) and confidentiality or integrity (sensitivity). A widely shared roster rates low on both, so lighter controls fit. Spreadsheets are information assets.

bank.question: Which list best describes the scope of the parties CPS 234's policy framework must give direction to?
options: Only those employed under an Australian employment contract
The board, senior management and technology staff only, since other people have no security obligations under the standard
APRA, the OAIC and ASIC
Board, management, committees, staff, contractors, consultants, related parties, third parties and customers
bank.explanation: The standard's note on the policy framework lists governing bodies and individuals with security roles plus all other staff, contractors, consultants, related parties, third parties and customers.

bank.question: A bank's security team says, 'We set our controls in 2019 to meet CPS 234, so we're compliant.' Which duty is most at risk?
options: Notifying APRA of material incidents within 72 hours of the board's first briefing on them
Classifying assets by criticality and sensitivity
Actively maintaining the capability as vulnerabilities, threats, assets and the business change
Defining the roles of the board
bank.explanation: CPS 234 requires the bank to actively maintain its capability in response to changing vulnerabilities and threats, including changes to assets and the business environment. A 2019 snapshot does not meet that.

bank.question: Which of these is an 'information security incident' under CPS 234?
options: A potential compromise, such as malware found on a server before any data is touched
Only a confirmed theft of customer data
Only an incident reported in the media
Only an attack by a foreign state
bank.explanation: The standard defines an incident as an actual or potential compromise of information security, so a potential compromise counts. Whether it must be notified is a separate materiality question.

bank.question: A bank's critical lending data is processed by a related company in the same group. What does CPS 234 require?
options: Nothing beyond the group's own audit, because related parties inside the same group are outside the standard's third-party rules
Only a yearly letter of comfort from the related party
Transfer the data back in-house within 12 months
Classify, protect and test those assets as if managed by any third party, including assessing the related party's capability
bank.explanation: CPS 234 applies to information assets managed by related parties as well as third parties: capability assessment, classification, control design evaluation, testing and assurance all apply.

bank.question: In June 2023 APRA applied a capital adjustment to Medibank after its cyber incident. What condition did APRA set for removing it?
options: Payment of a fine to the OAIC
Completion of an agreed remediation program to APRA's satisfaction
A change in Medibank's external auditor
The passing of 12 months without a new incident
bank.explanation: APRA said the AUD 250 million adjustment would stay until Medibank completed an agreed remediation program to APRA's satisfaction.

bank.question: Which statement about the RI Advice judgment is accurate?
options: The court held that licensees cannot be liable for cyber incidents occurring at the practices of their authorised representatives, only for their own systems
The court said cyber risk cannot be removed but can be materially reduced to an acceptable level with adequate documentation and controls
The court ordered compensation to every client
The court found APRA had failed to supervise RI Advice
bank.explanation: Justice Rofe observed that cyber risk cannot be reduced to zero but can be materially reduced with adequate documentation and controls. The licensee was held responsible for inadequate risk management across its network.

bank.question: Ransomware is detected on a Tuesday at 3 pm, and the incident lead decides on Wednesday at 9 am that it is material. Which statement best reflects CPS 234's notice duty?
options: The bank has 72 hours from the incident lead's materiality decision, so it may notify as late as Saturday at 9 am without any concern
The bank has 10 business days because it is a control weakness
No notice is needed until data loss is confirmed
Notify as soon as possible; the outer limit runs 72 hours from becoming aware of the incident, not from the materiality decision
bank.explanation: CPS 234 runs the 72 hours from when the bank becomes aware of the incident, and requires notice as soon as possible. Treating the clock as starting at a later internal decision risks a late notice.

bank.question: An independent test finds a material weakness. The bank expects to fix it within a week. What is the most accurate position under CPS 234?
options: The 10-business-day notice applies to weaknesses the bank expects it cannot remediate in a timely way, so it may not be triggered
APRA must be notified within 72 hours as an incident
Every test finding, whatever its rating or fix date, must be notified to APRA within 10 business days of the final report
The finding must be kept from the board until fixed
bank.explanation: The weakness notice targets material weaknesses the bank expects it cannot fix in time. A quick fix may not trigger it, but escalation and records still matter.

bank.question: Which arrangement best meets CPS 234's requirement for functionally independent testing?
options: The system's own developers testing their code
The vendor that built the system, under its own scope
A specialist testing team separate from the developers and operators of the control
An annual self-assessment by the business owner
bank.explanation: Testing must be carried out by appropriately skilled and functionally independent specialists. People who build or operate the control are not independent of it.

bank.question: A bank relies on its cloud provider's own penetration testing for a critical system. What does CPS 234 require?
options: Accept the provider's testing without review, because the provider is responsible for its own controls under the contract
Ban the provider from testing its own systems
Ask APRA to test the provider
Assess whether the provider's testing nature and frequency match the risk factors the standard lists
bank.explanation: Where the bank relies on a third party's control testing, it must assess whether the nature and frequency of that testing is commensurate with the factors listed in the standard.

bank.question: What must the bank's internal audit cover under CPS 234?
options: Only the financial cost of the security function
Design and operating effectiveness of security controls, including those run by related parties and third parties
Only controls the bank built and runs itself, since providers' controls are covered by their own auditors
Only the annual awareness training completion rate
bank.explanation: Internal audit must review the design and operating effectiveness of security controls, including those maintained by related and third parties, using appropriately skilled personnel.

bank.question: How often must the sufficiency of the CPS 234 testing program be reviewed?
options: At least annually, or when there is a material change to assets or the business environment
Every three years
Only when APRA requests it
Only after a material incident
bank.explanation: CPS 234 requires the program's sufficiency to be reviewed at least annually or after material change.

bank.question: A bank's incident response plan was last tested two years ago. Which CPS 234 duty is breached?
options: Notification of control weaknesses within 10 business days
Classification of assets by sensitivity
Annual review and testing of information security response plans
Defining the board's role
bank.explanation: Response plans must be reviewed and tested annually so they remain effective and fit for purpose.

bank.question: In the FIIG case, what did FIIG admit about detection?
options: The breach could not have been detected by any means
It detected the breach within minutes
Adequate measures suited to its size and data would have enabled it to detect and respond sooner
Detection was the responsibility of its clients
bank.explanation: FIIG admitted adequate cyber security measures would have let it detect and respond to the breach sooner, and that following its own policies could have supported earlier detection.

bank.question: Which approach to testing frequency fits CPS 234 best?
options: More frequent and deeper testing for assets with high criticality, sensitivity, fast-changing threats or untrusted exposure
The same annual penetration test for every system, regardless of risk, so that all results can be compared across the bank
Testing only systems that have failed before
Testing only after a software release
bank.explanation: CPS 234 ties nature and frequency of testing to the rate of change of threats, criticality and sensitivity, consequences, untrusted environments and frequency of change.

bank.question: Which statement about awareness training is most accurate for an Australian bank?
options: CPS 234 sets a fixed number of training hours per year
CPS 234 requires capability and controls; CPG 234 guidance describes an awareness program as sound practice
The Privacy Act requires a specific annual security course
APRA approves each bank's training content in advance, and CPS 234 sets the minimum hours and the pass mark
bank.explanation: Training is not prescribed as a separate course in CPS 234. CPG 234 describes sound practice, and APP 11.3 refers to organisational measures without naming a course.

bank.question: A bank's awareness program only records completions. Which CPG 234 sound practice is missing?
options: Sending all staff on external university courses
Publishing staff results on the website
Having APRA mark the tests
Testing understanding of the security policies, on commencement and periodically
bank.explanation: CPG 234 describes tracking training and testing understanding of relevant policies both on commencement and periodically. Completion alone does not show understanding.

bank.question: A contractor with system access is excluded from the bank's awareness program because 'they are not staff'. How does this sit with CPG 234?
options: Poorly: the guidance describes training for staff, contractors and third parties
Correctly: contractors are trained by their employer only
Correctly: CPS 234 excludes contractors
Poorly: contractors must be trained by APRA
bank.explanation: CPG 234 describes communicating security expectations to staff, contractors and third parties. CPS 234's policy framework also reaches contractors.

bank.question: An employee receives dozens of login approval prompts at midnight and finally approves one. What is this attack called?
options: Tailgating
Smishing
MFA fatigue
Credential stuffing
bank.explanation: MFA fatigue floods a user with approval prompts hoping they accept one. The right response is to deny and report immediately.

bank.question: A supplier calls a payments officer, gives a correct invoice number and asks to change bank details today. What is the best control?
options: Make the change if the invoice number matches
Ask the caller to send the request by email from the supplier's domain, then make the change once it arrives
Change it and check with the supplier next month
Verify the change by calling the supplier on a number already held on file, not one given in the call
bank.explanation: Invoice numbers and emails can be stolen or spoofed. Call-back verification through an independent, known channel defeats the pretext.

bank.question: Which CPG 234 testing technique checks how staff respond to attackers who target people?
options: Key management reviews
Social engineering tests
Firewall rule audits
Code vulnerability scans
bank.explanation: CPG 234 lists social engineering tests as an approach for testing controls such as access limitation and employee awareness.

bank.question: In APRA's June 2025 letter, what did APRA require from trustees whose authentication controls were deficient?
options: Immediate closure of every member account that had been accessed without MFA until a forensic review was complete
A public apology on their websites
Replacement of all directors
A material control weakness notification under CPS 234, or a clear rationale for why the gap was not material
bank.explanation: APRA required either a material control weakness notification or a clear rationale explaining why the issue was not material, plus a breach assessment where a weakness was notified.

bank.question: The same APRA letter asked trustees to identify which people in relation to CPS 234 compliance?
options: Their external auditors only
Their largest members
Their Accountable Person(s) under the Financial Accountability Regime
The OAIC case officer
bank.explanation: APRA asked each trustee to advise its Accountable Person(s) under FAR responsible for CPS 234 compliance, linking cyber controls to individual accountability.

bank.question: A bank keeps loan application files for rejected applicants indefinitely 'in case they are useful'. No law requires it. Which APP is most at risk?
options: APP 12, which gives people access to the information held about them and so requires keeping it indefinitely
APP 11.2, which requires reasonable steps to destroy or de-identify information no longer needed
APP 8, which covers sending data overseas
APP 1, which requires a privacy policy
bank.explanation: APP 11.2 requires destroying or de-identifying personal information no longer needed for a permitted purpose, unless law or court order requires it to be kept.

bank.question: Staff are emailing customer files to personal accounts to work from home. Which Privacy Act duty is most engaged?
options: APP 11.1 reasonable steps, including organisational measures such as policy, training and email controls
APP 13, which requires correcting personal information, together with the duty to notify APRA within 72 hours
The duty to notify APRA within 24 hours
APP 12 access requests
bank.explanation: This exposes personal information to unauthorised access and loss. APP 11.1, read with 11.3, expects technical and organisational measures to prevent it.

bank.question: A stolen laptop held customer tax file numbers. It was encrypted, but the password was written on a note in the laptop bag. How does section 26WG's encryption factor apply?
options: Encryption means the breach can never be eligible
The key was exposed, so the encryption is likely to be overcome and serious harm is more likely
Only the laptop's value matters
Tax file numbers are not personal information
bank.explanation: Section 26WG asks how likely security measures are to be overcome and notes a key as information needed to circumvent encryption. Exposing the password undermines the protection.

bank.question: Within an hour of a misdirected email, the bank gets credible written confirmation the recipient deleted it unopened. What does section 26WF provide?
options: The breach must still be notified to the Commissioner and to all customers, because the email was sent and the disclosure happened
The bank must notify APRA instead of the Commissioner
The recipient must notify the Commissioner
If remedial action means serious harm is no longer likely, the disclosure is treated as never having been an eligible breach
bank.explanation: Under section 26WF, remedial action taken before serious harm that makes harm no longer likely means the access or disclosure is not, and never was, an eligible data breach.

bank.question: A bank has reasonable grounds to believe an eligible data breach occurred. Which order of actions fits sections 26WK and 26WL?
options: Notify individuals after the 30-day assessment, then the Commissioner at year end
Notify APRA only, because APRA passes eligible data breach notices for banks on to the Commissioner, who then notifies customers
Prepare the statement and give it to the Commissioner as soon as practicable, then notify individuals as soon as practicable
Publish on the website first, then decide whether a statement is needed
bank.explanation: Section 26WK requires the statement to be given to the Commissioner as soon as practicable; section 26WL then requires notifying individuals as soon as practicable after the statement is prepared.

bank.question: A bank sent personal information to an overseas processor under APP 8. The processor suffers a breach. Is the bank inside Part IIIC?
options: Yes: in these circumstances the Act treats the information as held by the bank for the scheme
No: overseas breaches are outside the Act
Only if the processor is APRA-regulated
Only if the customers live overseas
bank.explanation: Section 26WC deems the APP entity to hold personal information disclosed to an overseas recipient where APP 8.1 applied, so the bank must deal with the breach under Part IIIC.

bank.question: A breach affects 50,000 customers but only 2,000 are at risk of serious harm. Under section 26WL, which option is open to the bank?
options: Notify the contents of the statement to the 2,000 at-risk individuals, if that is practicable
Notify only those who complain
Notify no one, because most of the affected customers are not at risk and the scheme looks at the whole group
Notify the Commissioner and wait for a direction
bank.explanation: Section 26WL allows notifying all affected individuals or, if practicable, only those at risk; publishing is the fallback when neither is practicable.

bank.question: Who regulates the Privacy Act and the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme?
options: APRA
The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
ASIC
AUSTRAC

bank.question: A bank says its customer enquiries line is not a critical operation because it is 'just a call centre'. What does CPS 230 say?
options: Call centres are outside CPS 230
Only APRA may decide what is critical
Customer enquiries are critical only for insurers
Customer enquiries are a minimum critical operation for all entities unless the bank can justify otherwise
bank.explanation: CPS 230 lists customer enquiries, and the systems and infrastructure supporting critical operations, as minimum critical operations for all APRA-regulated entities unless justified otherwise.

bank.question: Which statement about tolerance levels under CPS 230 is correct?
options: APRA sets identical tolerance levels for all banks in a schedule to the standard, and banks may not set their own
Tolerance levels are optional for small banks
The bank sets them for each critical operation, the board approves them, and APRA may require changes or set them
Management sets them without board involvement
bank.explanation: Banks set tolerance levels for time, data loss and minimum service; the board approves them; APRA may require a review, and may set levels where it sees heightened risk.

bank.question: Which of these is an operational risk that CPS 230 expressly includes?
options: Interest rate risk in the banking book
Credit spread risk
Equity market risk
Conduct risk
bank.explanation: CPS 230 lists legal, regulatory, compliance, conduct, technology, data and change management risk among the operational risks to manage. The others are financial risks managed under other standards.

bank.question: A bank uses a central bank's settlement service on standard terms it cannot negotiate. How did the 2026 CPS 230 amendments affect this?
options: Certain contract requirements need not be met for listed provider categories, such as central banks, using standardised terms
The service no longer counts as an arrangement at all
The bank must stop using the service
The bank must still negotiate custom terms covering audit access, APRA access and termination with the central bank
bank.explanation: The amended CPS 230 exempts arrangements with listed categories, including central banks, from certain agreement requirements where standardised terms are used or there is no formal agreement.

bank.question: What must the BCP include under CPS 230?
options: Only the IT disaster recovery runbooks for the core banking platform, signed off by the chief technology officer each quarter
A list of staff home addresses
Register of critical operations and tolerances, triggers, actions, execution risks and dependencies, and a communications strategy
The bank's marketing calendar
bank.explanation: CPS 230 sets these BCP contents; disaster recovery for critical information assets sits within a broader plan.

bank.question: What must internal audit do in relation to a proposed material arrangement that outsources a critical operation?
options: Approve the arrangement in place of the board, and then run the provider's monitoring for the life of the contract
Review the proposed arrangement and regularly report on compliance with the service provider policy
Run the outsourced service itself
Nothing until after the contract ends
bank.explanation: CPS 230 requires internal audit to review any proposed material arrangement outsourcing a critical operation and to report regularly to the board or audit committee on compliance with the policy.

bank.question: How often must a bank submit its register of material service providers to APRA?
options: Monthly
Only when APRA asks
Annually
Every three years
bank.explanation: CPS 230 requires the register to be submitted to APRA on an annual basis.

bank.question: An internal auditor preparing for APRA review asks for evidence on the human side of security. Which set is most useful?
options: Staff holiday rosters and canteen menus
Training completion and understanding test results, phishing trends, policy sign-offs and incident reporting data
The vendor's brochures
The number of emails in each inbox
bank.explanation: CPG 234 describes tracked training, tested understanding and periodic policy sign-off, and gives phishing and awareness metrics as examples for board reporting.
